subject: Post-call: Model fit scoping & parity gating — Ambassador.ai
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@ambassador.ai>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@ambassador.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-08-09T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Model fit scoping & parity gating — Ambassador.ai

Thanks for the call today — quick recap and recommended next steps so we have an actionable plan. Appreciate you walking through the sample tasks and the baseline behavior for AmbassadorModel v2.

Recap (short):
- Goal: Replace or match AmbassModel v2 for FAQ routing + short-answer extraction with an open-model candidate to reduce cost and vendor lock.
- Key acceptance criteria discussed: precision/recall for entity extraction, answer F1 on the public test set, regression tolerance relative to baseline, and 95th-percentile latency.
- Data: you shared a 8k-sample anonymized set; we asked for a few edge-case documents (rare intents).

Recommended next steps (we can kick these off if you confirm):
1) Evaluation plan: Redwood runs a parity pass over your 8k set plus 500 synthetic edge cases. Deliverables: metric report + per-example diffs.
2) Models to trial (initial):
   - Open candidates: LlamaX-13B-q4f32 (quantized variant), Mistral-instruct-7B.
   - Proprietary baseline: AmbassadorModel v2 (as supplied).
3) Acceptance thresholds (proposal):
   - Intent classification F1 >= 0.78 (relative delta <= -0.03 vs baseline allowed for cost tradeoffs).
   - Answer F1 >= 0.80 and Rouge-L within 0.04 of baseline.
   - 95p latency <= 250 ms for 512-token budget in your target region.
4) Risk gating / quality regression concerns:
   - Flag any drop >5% absolute on critical intents; require canary with human-in-the-loop for first 2 weeks.
5) Logistics: upload final evaluation bundle (CSV + prompt set) or grant us access to a shared Drive link.

Attachments and links included in this email: parity_matrix.xlsx (proposed metric matrix), prompt_set_v1.jsonl (seed prompts). Also linking our internal run template: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-demo-benchmarks and HubSpot HS-11234 for the opportunity.

Questions for you before we run:
- Which metric (F1, EM, Rouge-L) is most important for legal/accuracy signoff?
- Do you want cost-per-inference estimates included in the first pass?
- Can you confirm a contact for security/compliance checklist (SOC2 evidence) for the private trial?

Proposed timeline: parity run + report in 5 business days after we get the final bundle and access.

Thanks — looking forward.

—
Olga Petrov
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Date: 2025-08-10T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit scoping & parity gating — Ambassador.ai

Thanks, Olga — this is helpful. Quick answers inline and a couple of asks.

> Which metric (F1, EM, Rouge-L) is most important for legal/accuracy signoff?
Our compliance team focuses on precision and F1 for extracted entities (we prefer conservative answers). For downstream routing accuracy, recall on rare intents is also important.

> Do you want cost-per-inference estimates included in the first pass?
Yes — please include a ballpark cost delta vs our current footprint (p50 token cost & p95 request cost).

> Security contact for SOC2 evidence?
Looping in Priya (CC) who owns security/compliance. Priya, can you confirm whether we should share a redacted logs extract or if we need an NDA first?

Two other asks from my side:
- Can you include a short-run that uses our in-house prompt templates (I attached one example in the call).
- Also, can Redwood show a simple canary rollout plan (how you'd run open model in parallel to baseline and escalate if regressions found)?

Jordan
Director, Product — Ambassador.ai
jordan.miles@ambassador.ai
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@ambassador.ai>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@ambassador.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-08-10T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit scoping & parity gating — Ambassador.ai

Appreciate the quick reply, Jordan — answers below and attachments included.

Security/NDA: if you prefer, we can operate under a short SCA (data-sharing agreement) + limited-use MSA appendix. Priya: happy to sync 15 min to confirm the exact artifact set.

Cost estimates: yes — we'll include p50/p95 token cost estimates for each candidate model (inc. quantized variants) in the parity report. Expect an initial cost delta table in the first deliverable.

Canary rollout: attached eval-instructions.md and a sample MOP-benchmark-run-20250809.csv that shows how we instrumented the run on a mocked traffic slice. In short:
- Phase 0: offline parity on your 8k + 500 edge cases.
- Phase 1 (canary): route 2% of live traffic to open candidate behind a holdout check; compare per-request diffs and surface regressions to Ops.
- Phase 2: expand to 25% with auto-fallback to baseline for flagged intents (human in loop on flagged requests).
- Phase 3: full cutover if acceptance gates satisfied for 14 days.

I attached: MOP-benchmark-run-20250809.csv (sample run CSV), eval-instructions.md (runbook), plus the parity_matrix.xlsx and prompt_set_v1.jsonl from yesterday.

Next steps for us: please confirm that we have access to the final anonymized bundle (S3 link or Drive folder) and confirm the metric priority (F1 vs strict precision). Once confirmed we'll kick the parity pass.

—
Olga

Adding a few technical guardrails from the SE perspective — high-level notes so Jordan/Priya know what we'll watch for during the parity run:

- Quality regression concerns to surface immediately:
  * Intent flip: when the model assigns a different top intent vs baseline for high-priority intents.
  * Hallucination on short-answer extraction (we'll compute hallucination rate vs ground truth).
  * Tokenization edge cases (non-ASCII, punctuation-heavy samples).
- Suggested acceptance gates (refining Olga's proposal):
  * Critical intents: no more than 2% absolute drop in F1.
  * Average answer F1: >= 0.80 but allow 3% lower if 20%+ cost savings observed.
  * Latency SLO: p95 <= 250 ms; if open model exceeds by >50 ms we require a perf plan.
- Canary instrumentation: per-token cost, per-request delta, a small human review queue (10/day).

I'll prepare a short canary playbook (one-pager) and drop it in the Drive link. If Jordan/Priya want, we can also include a short demo that shows a side-by-side comparison of AmbassModel v2 vs LlamaX outputs for 30 sample queries.

—
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
